summary: Ramified equal-part merging links finite-field factor degrees to the faithful polynomial Galois action. A general probability law on partitions then excludes every transitive permutation subgroup other than the alternating and symmetric groups. The plan includes the higher irreducibility adapter, the actual primitive minimum-degree proofs, and the strengthened long-part event needed to repair the imprimitive argument.

nodes.title: Bounded equal-part merging
nodes.statement: For real y≥1 and partitions a,b of the same integer, EqualPartMerging y a.parts b.parts holds iff the occurrences of a are partitioned into nonempty blocks, each of cardinal≤y, all entries in a block equal, and b is the multiset of their sums. A witness is a multiset of multisets whose flattening is a and whose multiset of sums is b. The raw-multiset relation also handles the empty partition.
proofSteps: Use occurrence blocks, not a set of lengths, so repetitions are retained. Nonemptiness prohibits creating zero parts.
Each block with length k and cardinal m contributes m·k, and 1≤m≤y; flattening proves total-sum conservation.

nodes.title: Cycle lengths over cyclic fibres
nodes.statement: Let finite nonempty X map surjectively and equivariantly to Y under permutations σ,ψ. Suppose ψ has one full cycle of length d>0 and every fibre has m>0 points. Then each σ-orbit has length d·m_i with1≤m_i≤m, meets each fibre in exactly m_i points, and Σ_i m_i=m. Consequently fullCycleType σ is an m-merging of the multiset containing m copies of d.
proofSteps: The first return to a chosen fibre is σ^d. Its disjoint orbits have cardinalities m_i and partition that fibre.
Going around the d bottom points transports each return orbit bijectively; its full σ-orbit has d·m_i points.
The identity Σ_i m_i=m supplies the complete merging witness, not just a bound on individual cycle lengths.

nodes.title: Maximum irreducible-factor multiplicity
nodes.statement: For a polynomial f over a field, maxFactorMultiplicity f is the maximum count of an irreducible normalized factor in normalizedFactors f, with maximum0 on the empty list. Thus units and the library’s empty normalizedFactors convention at0 have value0; its arithmetic use always has nonzero monic reduction. Distinct factors of the same degree are not identified.
proofSteps: Take the finite supremum of the count function over the factors’ finset.
For nonzero nonunits, UFD factorization identifies these counts with the largest exponent m for which an irreducible q satisfies q^m∣f.

nodes.title: Reduction fibres count root multiplicities
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, a field K, a ring homomorphism r:R→K, a finite set S⊆R and z∈K, the root multiplicity of z in ∏_{x∈S}(X−r(x)) equals #{x∈S:r(x)=z}. In the integral-root application, for each irreducible q dividing A mod p with exponent m, every residue root of q has exactly m integral roots of A above it.
proofSteps: The factors X−r(x) are nonzero. Add root multiplicities through the finite product: each contributes1 or0.

For the arithmetic application, factor A mod p in its splitting residue field. Irreducible finite-field factors are separable and different factors have disjoint root sets, so the multiplicity at a root of q is precisely q’s exponent.

nodes.title: Ramified Frobenius merging theorem
nodes.statement: Let A∈ℤ[X] be monic of degree n>0, with its image in ℚ[X] separable, and let p be any prime. Put M=maxFactorMultiplicity(A mod p). There exists σ in Gal(A/ℚ) whose faithful action on the n roots has fullCycleType an M-merging of Polynomial.factorDegrees A p. There is no squarefree-reduction, discriminant or unramified-prime hypothesis.
proofSteps: Monicity makes each splitting-field root integral over ℤ. Separability lists n distinct roots; mapping the product of their linear factors to the residue field gives the reduction polynomial.
Choose a maximal ideal of the ring of integers above(p), using the pinned lying-over theorem. The existing arithmetic Frobenius lift at this ideal acts equivariantly on root-reduction fibres.
For an irreducible factor q of degree d and multiplicity m, the pinned finite-field theorem identifies a d-cycle of residue roots, and the fibre-cardinality identity gives m roots per fibre.
Apply equivariant-cycle-fibres on each such component; concatenate the blocks. Since m≤M, the full root permutation is an M-merging of the repeated factor-degree multiset.

acceptance: A=X²−2 at p=2 has repeated factor X² and M=2, so the theorem must elaborate without an unramified hypothesis.
For monic squarefree reduction M=1, the conclusion specializes to exact factorDegrees=fullCycleType.
Degree0 is excluded here; units have empty factors and M=0 rather than an undefined maximum.

nodes.title: Polynomial over a tuple root field
nodes.statement: For f∈F[X] over a field and an injection x:Fin j→roots(f) in its splitting field L, let K_x=F(adjoin range x). Define tupleRootQuotient f x as f mapped to K_x, divided monically by ∏_{i<j}(X−x_i) formed in K_x. For separable f, the division is exact; mapping back to L gives the remaining-root polynomial.
proofSteps: Use IntermediateField.adjoin for K_x; each selected root belongs by the existing subset_adjoin inclusion.
The selected roots are distinct because x is an injection. Divide by their monic linear-factor product.
Separability and exact factorization identify the complement roots and degree deg f−j, and prove the quotient separable and split in L.

nodes.title: Tuple stabilizer and root-generated field
nodes.statement: For an injection x of j roots of f into its splitting field L, the stabilizer of x for the componentwise Gal(f/F) action on embeddings equals K_x.fixingSubgroup. Restricting this stabilizer to L over K_x identifies its faithful action on unselected roots with the Galois action needed by the quotient irreducibility test.
proofSteps: An automorphism fixes the tuple iff it fixes every selected root.
Fixing the selected generators is equivalent to fixing their intermediate-field adjoin; use the Galois correspondence and extend embeddings inside the normal splitting field.
The quotient splits in L, which need not be its minimal splitting field. Use the surjective restriction of automorphisms to that splitting field, so orbit transitivity descends and lifts.

nodes.title: Three-premise partition law
nodes.statement: For a probability measure ν on Nat.Partition n (discrete measurable space), constants C≥1,0<t<1,0<κ≤1,0<δ≤1/10 define PartitionLaw by three bounds: (a) ν({k,ℓ}≤ρ.parts)≤C/(kℓ) for integers2≤k,ℓ≤n/4, requiring two occurrences if k=ℓ; (b) ν(∃U≤ρ.parts,ΣU=k)≤C k^(−δ) for integers n^(1−δ/2)≤k≤n/2; (c) for f:ℕ→{0,1},1≤m≤n/log n, L=Σ_{k=1}^m f(k)/k, ν(Σ_{k∈ρ.parts,k≤m} f(k)≤tL)≤C exp(−κL). The last sum counts occurrences, and all displayed endpoints are inclusive integer cutoffs.
proofSteps: Record the real-parameter ranges as proposition fields and write the three event bounds as genuine quantified mathematical conditions.
Use the existing probability measure, finite partition type and real-valued event measure. Indicators are Bool-valued; harmonicMass is the displayed finite sum notation.

nodes.title: Five partition anatomy events
nodes.statement: For n,t,κ,δ,α real parameters and a partitionρ, GoodEvent i (i=0,…,4) is E₁,…,E₅*: E₁ forbids occurrence pairs k,ℓ≤n/4 with gcd(k,ℓ)≥n^(κα); E₂ forbids a submultiset sum nj/r for r∣n,2≤r≤n^(δ/2),1≤j<r; E₃ requires at least(αt/2)log n parts in[n^(1−α),n/log n]; E₄ requires at least(t/4)log n parts k≤√n/3 with a prime divisor p>n^(1/8); E₅* requires, for each integer r≥2, at least FOUR parts in[n^(1−2α),n/log n] not divisible by r. Every count retains multiplicity. During the criterion α=δ/4−θ/2∈[ε/2,1/40].
proofSteps: Use integer parts and real cutoff comparisons; E₂ retains δ/2 independently of α.
Strengthen the source’s single-witness E₅ to four occurrences. E₁ makes sufficiently long counted parts distinct at the asymptotic thresholds used in the proof.

nodes.title: Uniform long-interval harmonic masses
nodes.statement: Fix ε>0. Uniformly for α∈[ε/2,1/40] and sufficiently large n, the harmonic mass of integers in[n^(1−α),n/log n] is α log n−log log n+O_ε(1). For2≤r≤n^α, the harmonic mass in[n^(1−2α),n/log n] not divisible by r is(1−1/r)(2α log n−log log n)+O_ε(1), uniformly in r. Floor/ceiling changes are included in the error.
proofSteps: Subtract upper/lower harmonic-sum bounds at the inclusive integer endpoints. Their differences from logarithms are uniformly bounded.

For divisible parts put k=rj and subtract(1/r) times the corresponding harmonic interval; r≤n^α ensures the lower endpoint stays≥n^(1−3α), so no empty or below1 cutoff invalidates the logarithm calculation.

nodes.title: Harmonic mass of parts with a large prime factor
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently large n, Σ_{1≤k≤√n/3, ∃p prime:p∣k,p>n^(1/8)}1/k ≥(log n)/4. In fact the sum is at least(1/2−e^γ/8)log n+O(1), where γ is the existing Euler constant; e^γ<2 makes the coefficient strictly greater than1/4.
proofSteps: The total harmonic mass through √n/3 is(1/2)log n+O(1).
Every integer whose prime factors are≤n^(1/8) contributes to the full positive reciprocal Euler product over those primes, which is an upper bound even without a size cutoff.
Invoke exactly the imported Mertens product with leading constant e^γ, and the standard Euler-constant bound γ<log2. A generic O(log x) comparison has no sufficient coefficient.

nodes.title: Large-gcd pair probability

nodes.title: Connectivity of primitive orbital graphs
nodes.statement: For a primitive permutation subgroup G on a finite carrier and x≠y, the undirected relation joining u,v when(u,v) or(v,u) belongs to the G-orbit of(x,y) is connected: every a,b are related by its reflexive transitive closure.

Primitivity makes a component either a singleton or the whole carrier; the non-diagonal edge excludes the singleton case for its endpoints, and transitivity excludes singleton components elsewhere.

Translating vertices or endpoint pairs gives bijections proving valency and intersection-count constancy. These are proof infrastructure for the next target, not a new general coherent-configuration library.

nodes.title: Babai’s distinguisher lower bound
nodes.statement: Let G≤Sym(α) be primitive but not2-pretransitive, with n=card α≥5. For every x≠y, #{z:no element of G fixes z and sends x to y}≥√n/2. Hence every nonidentity element has support at least√n/2.
proofSteps: Work with the diagonal pair orbits as colours. Their non-diagonal valencies ρ_i and distinguisher numbers D(i) are constant by orbit transport.

For a noncomplete symmetrized orbital graph its COMPLEMENT has diameter2 (Babai Lemma8.5); the regular diameter-two count gives ρ_i≤n−1−√(n−1). If the symmetrization is complete, the paired valency is(n−1)/2. Counting triples gives average distinguisher number Dbar≥n−ρmax>√n.
Along an orbital path, D(a,b) lies in the union of the edge distinguisher sets. Thus if a symmetrized orbital has diameter2, D(i)≥Dbar/2>√n/2.
If its diameter≥3, a shortest path of length3 has disjoint endpoint neighborhoods, both contained in D(a,b); the path union bound gives D(i)≥2ρ_i/3.

For fixed z, form the weighted graph of z’s suborbits joined by orbital-i edges. Connectivity follows from the orbital graph. A spanning tree, oriented away from the singleton suborbit, has total weight≥n−1 because the edge between suborbits of valencies ρ_j,ρ_k has weight≥max(ρ_j,ρ_k).
Double-count distinguished ordered orbital-i pairs to get D(i)≥(n−1)/ρ_i. Combining with2ρ_i/3 yields D(i)²≥2(n−1)/3>n/4.
Use D(x,gx)⊆support g for a moved point x. No group-order or base-size estimate is substituted for the support theorem.

nodes.title: Bochert’s doubly transitive minimum degree
nodes.statement: For a2-pretransitive subgroup G≤Sym(α) of degree n≥38 that does not contain alternatingGroup α, minSupport G=some m implies m≥n/4.
proofSteps: The imported primitive3-cycle/transposition recognition excludes m≤3. Choose u of minimal support m>3, a moved α and β=uα. The case m=n already satisfies the bound.

Conjugate u by the stabilizer of α. Double transitivity makes its action on the other n−1 points transitive, so the fraction of conjugates fixing β is(n−m)/(n−1), and the fraction moving any specified γ≠α is(m−1)/(n−1). These proportions follow by counting an invariant incidence relation in both orders (Schomburg Lemmas2.3–2.5).
Every conjugate v fixing β moves α and fails to commute with u. The commutator has support contained in Δ∪uΔ∪vΔ, Δ=support u∩support v. Minimality gives|Δ|≥m/3.
Sum|Δ| over these conjugates. The upper bound is their cardinal plus(m−2) times the total conjugate cardinal times(m−1)/(n−1). Cancel the nonempty conjugacy-class factor to obtain n≤4m+6/(m−3).
If n≥38 then m≥10; the final correction is≤6/7, and integrality gives m≥n/4.

nodes.title: Cycle arithmetic in a block orbit
nodes.statement: Let a permutationσ preserve a block system of r blocks of common cardinal s. A point cycle L of lengthℓ meets one block orbit of size r′ and has s′ points in each of these blocks, where1≤r′≤r,1≤s′≤s,ℓ=r′s′. The union X of these blocks isσ-invariant of cardinal r′s, and every point cycle in X has length divisible by r′. Different point cycles have either equal or disjoint block orbits. This includes singleton cycles.
proofSteps: Represent the block system as a surjective equivariant quotient b:X→Fin r with all fibres of cardinal s, importing the parent’s block-system construction.
The projected σ-orbit is exactly the orbit of its block under the induced permutation. Equivariance bijects its intersections with the blocks.
A σ-cycle in the same block orbit visits every block in that orbit; its length is a positive multiple of r′. Block orbits partition the blocks, proving the equal-or-disjoint dichotomy.

nodes.title: Exclusion of proper primitive groups
nodes.statement: Fix0<t,0<κ≤1,0<δ≤1/10 and0<ε<δ/2. Uniformly in θ∈[0,δ/2−ε] and sufficiently large n, ifρ∈E₁∩E₄, then no n^(1/8)-merging ofρ belongs to a primitive subgroup unequal to A_n and S_n. In particular this excludes n^θ-mergings since θ≤1/20<1/8.
proofSteps: There are at most three original parts>n/4. Each has at most eight prime divisors>n^(1/8), so at most24 exceptional primes arise.

E₁ permits at most one small part divisible by each such prime. E₄ supplies(t/4)log n distinct parts k≤√n/3 with a prime factor>n^(1/8); for large n choose one not meeting these exceptional primes. Its chosen prime p divides no other original part.
The selected k has multiplicity1 and survives any allowed equal-part merging. Other output lengths are mℓ with m≤n^(1/8)

Raise the merged permutation to p^(v_p(k)−1) times the prime-to-p part of the least common multiple of its cycle lengths. All other cycles die; the k-cycle remains nonidentity and moves exactly k points, by the pinned cycle-power support theorem.
Its support≤√n/3<(√n−1)/2 for n>9 contradicts primitive minimum degree. The required comparison is n^(κα)≤n^(1/40)<n^(1/8)<p.

acceptance: No Frobenius or probability-law assumption enters this deterministic combinatorial theorem.
The exponent kills every other cycle and does not kill the chosen one; a claim of a single p-cycle is unnecessary.

nodes.title: Exclusion of transitive imprimitive groups
nodes.statement: With the same parameter ranges and uniformity as primitive-exclusion, ifρ∈E₁∩E₂∩E₃∩E₄∩E₅*, no n^θ-merging ofρ belongs to any transitive imprimitive subgroup of S_n. E₄ is harmless in this statement but unused in its proof; E₅* is the strengthened four-part event.
proofSteps: Supposeσ preserves r equal blocks of size s=n/r with1<r<n, and put α=δ/4−θ/2. Long parts in the chosen intervals lie≤n/log n≤n/4 and≥n^(κα) for uniformly large n, so E₁ makes each unique and unchanged by merging.

If2≤r≤n^(δ/2), choose a long partℓ not divisible by r via E₅*. Its block orbit has r′<r. Its invariant union has size nr′/r. Pulling the contained cycle lengths back through merging yields a submultiset sum forbidden by E₂.

If n^(δ/2)<r<n^(1−α), choose FIVE distinct E₃ parts. For eachℓ, r′≥ℓ/s>n^(δ/2−α)>n^(κα). Two selected cycles cannot have the same block orbit, since their gcd would then be≥r′; thus their block unions are disjoint. At most one selected cycle fills its blocks, since s>n^α and two such lengths would violate E₁.

A permutation has at most three cycles>n/4. Of the five disjoint block unions, choose one whose selected cycle does not fill its blocks and that contains no cycle>n/4. It has a companion cycle m·k≤n/4, with k an original part and m≤n^θ. Then gcd(k,ℓ)≥r′/m>n^(δ/2−α−θ)=n^α≥n^(κα), contradicting E₁ within its actual small-part range.

If n^(1−α)≤r<n, then s≥2. Choose FOUR E₅* long parts not divisible by s. Each leaves unused points in its block orbit and has r′>n^(1−3α). Their block unions are disjoint by E₁; at most three contain a cycle>n/4.
In the fourth union choose a companion m·k≤n/4. Then gcd(k,ℓ)≥r′/n^θ>n^(1−3α−θ)≥n^(κα), again contradicting E₁. This repairs the unbounded-companion step while preserving the probability exponent.

nodes.title: Generalized Łuczak–Pyber criterion
nodes.statement: Fix C≥1,0<t<1,0<κ≤1,0<δ≤1/10,0<ε<δ/2. There are B≥0 and integer N≥3 depending only on C,t,κ,δ,ε such that, for every n≥N, every probability measureν on partitions of n satisfying PartitionLaw, and every θ∈[0,δ/2−ε], ν({ρ:∃σ∈BadTransitive(Fin n),σ∈MergePerms(n^θ)ρ})≤B(log n)² n^(−κ(δ/4−θ/2)). The law may vary with n; B and N do not depend on ν or θ.
proofSteps: On the intersection of the five good events the primitive and imprimitive exclusions leave no bad-transitive witness. Every permitted witness group is in one of these cases.
The bad event is therefore contained in the union of their complements. All events are measurable in the discrete finite partition space.
Use the five failure estimates. Since α≤δ/4,κ≤1, their powers and logarithmic factors are each bounded by a constant times(log n)² n^(−κα).
Take the maximum of the finitely many uniform thresholds and sum the constants. The α lower bound ε/2 makes this choice uniform up to θ=δ/2−ε.

nodes.title: Polynomial-side bad-group certificate
nodes.statement: Let A∈ℤ[X] be monic, separable and irreducible overℚ, and p prime. If the faithful root-action image is neither alternating nor symmetric and maxFactorMultiplicity(A mod p)≤y, then an element in that image witnesses a y-merging of A.factorDegrees p in the bad-transitive set on its n roots. Transporting the roots to Fin n gives the event bounded by generalized-luczak-pyber. Therefore any random-polynomial application bounds its bad-group event by the union of the large-multiplicity event and this partition event.
proofSteps: Irreducibility gives transitivity; characteristic0 and the stated separability give exactly n roots.
Ramified-merging supplies a Galois element. Monotonicity increases M to y; its image subgroup is a permitted bad-transitive witness.

Transport the finite root carrier to Fin n, preserving fullCycleType and the alternating/symmetric subgroup inequalities. The pointwise implication yields the event inclusion on any coefficient probability space.

Concrete laws, repeated-factor tails and quantitative irreducibility estimates are consumers supplied by ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials; no such theorem is an input to the arbitrary-law criterion.

sourceIssues.locator: proof of Lemma 12.9, Cases 2b and 3, p. 63 (arXiv v3; the author version of 24 May 2023 has the same text and pages; the published pagination was not seen)
sourceIssues.printed: In Case 2b, the source uses r_i′ | mk to infer gcd(r_i′, k) ⩾ r_i′/m > n^{δ/2−α−θ} = n^α, then gcd(k, ℓ_i) > n^α, claiming a contradiction to ρ ∈ E₁. In Case 3 it derives gcd(k, ℓ) ⩾ r′/m ⩾ r′/n^θ and again claims a contradiction to ρ ∈ E₁.
sourceIssues.correction: E₁ concerns only pairs of parts ≤ n/4, and nothing bounds the part k. Repair (this continuation): in Case 2 take five distinct parts ℓ ∈ ρ ∩ [n^{1−α}, n/log n] (E₁, E₃). The unions X_ℓ of the blocks met by their cycles are single block orbits of g, pairwise disjoint because X_ℓ = X_ℓ′ would force r_ℓ′ > n^α to divide ℓ and ℓ′. At most one ℓ has s_ℓ′ = s (Case 2a), and g has at most three cycles longer than n/4, so some ℓ has s_ℓ′ < s and only cycles of length ≤ n/4 in X_ℓ outside its own cycle; their parts k are ≤ n/4 and the printed argument applies. In Case 3 argue the same way with four parts ℓ ∈ ρ ∩ [n^{1−2α}, n/log n] not divisible by s, which a strengthened E₅ supplies with the same probability bound as Lemma 12.6.
sourceIssues.reason: The companion original part may exceed n/4, outside the exact E₁ hypothesis. Five middle-range block orbits and four large-range block orbits allow one to avoid every cycle longer than n/4. The four-part lower-tail estimate uses count≤3≤tL_r and retains the original rate.
